facts.fact_text: The applicant's conviction was based, inter alia, on his participation in several demonstrations.
The applicant did not deny that he had taken part in the demonstrations referred to by the Malatya public prosecutor.
The applicant argued that the demonstrations and press conferences in which he had participated had been legal activities permitted by the relevant authorities.

The Malatya Assize Court found that the applicant had taken part in a demonstration held on 7 December 2009 in protest against the allegedly deteriorating conditions of detention of the leader of the PKK.
The Malatya Assize Court found that the applicant had taken part in a press conference held in Tunceli on 7 March 2010 in the context of the centenary of International Women's Day.
The Malatya Assize Court found that the applicant had taken part in a march held on 1 May 2010 to celebrate International Workers' Day.

On 23 June 2011 the Malatya Assize Court convicted the applicant under Article 314 § 2 of the Turkish Criminal Code (Law no. 5237) of being a member of an armed terrorist organisation, namely the PKK (the Workers' Party of Kurdistan).
The Malatya Assize Court sentenced the applicant to nine years' imprisonment on 23 June 2011.

The bill of indictment filed by the Malatya public prosecutor on 10 June 2010 charged the applicant, along with eight others, with being a member of an armed terrorist organisation, namely the PKK (the Workers' Party of Kurdistan), under Article 314 § 2 of the Turkish Criminal Code (Law no. 5237).
The bill of indictment filed by the Malatya public prosecutor on 10 June 2010 also charged the applicant under section 5 of the Law on the Prevention of Terrorism.
